en.title: Can Swapping Letters Across the Whole String Reach the Target
en.description:
Each operation picks two distinct lowercase letters and swaps all of their occurrences in the whole string; one of the letters may currently be absent. For each pair of equal-length strings, decide whether the transformation is possible and output 1 or 0.

The standard I/O and the solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..100000), followed by n lines, each with two non-empty lowercase strings of equal length. Each string has length ≤200000, and the total length of all strings is ≤500000.
en.output: Output n values, each 0 or 1, in input order.
en.explanation: Example 1: swapping b and d is enough, so output 1. Example 2: swap z and p, then swap e and l, so output 1. Example 3: the two characters of ab cannot both become a, so output 0; aba can map to xyx, so output 1.
hints: Build, position by position, the mapping from source characters to target characters and the reverse mapping; a conflict in either direction makes it impossible, otherwise it is feasible.
